questions: Did your difficulty walking begin suddenly, within the last few hours or days?
Do you have weakness or numbness on one side of your body?
Have you had facial drooping, slurred speech, confusion, or trouble understanding speech?
Have you had a new severe headache, double vision, or loss of vision?
Do you feel dizzy or as though the room is spinning?
Have you lost control of your bladder or bowels, or developed numbness around your groin?
Do you have new severe neck or back pain?
Is walking limited by pain in your hips, knees, legs, or feet?
Do you notice shaking, stiffness, or unusually slow movements?
Have you had a similar walking problem before?
Do your walking difficulties vary substantially from one occasion to another?
Can you walk normally when you are alone or distracted?
Did this problem start after an injury, illness, or infection?
Have you recently started, stopped, or changed any medications or used alcohol or recreational drugs?
Have you previously been diagnosed with a neurological or muscular condition?

dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Anti-GQ1b IgG autoimmune neuropathy causing Miller Fisher syndrome (ophthalmoplegia–ataxia variant of Guillain–Barré syndrome)

ALTERNATIVE 1: Bickerstaff brainstem encephalitis due to anti-GQ1b antibodies

ALTERNATIVE 2: Progressive supranuclear palsy

ALTERNATIVE 3: Mitochondrial chronic progressive external ophthalmoplegia syndrome
